note: trial-068 combined --no-gradient-checkpointing with --lora-layers-to-transform 18 and OOM'd almost immediately (21.8s wall clock, 21.01GiB/22.03GiB allocated) - confirms gradient checkpointing is not optional at this depth (36 layers) and batch_size=8, it's essential to fit the VRAM budget, not just a nice-to-have (trial-067's 9.5GB peak WAS the checkpointed number, not headroom on top of an already-safe baseline). This trial reverts to trial-067's exact config (gradient_checkpointing back on) and adds ONLY --lora-layers-to-transform 18, isolating that variable cleanly against trial-067's 1705.3s baseline - unlike trial-068, which combined two changes and OOM'd before either could be measured. Should have equal or LOWER peak memory than trial-067 (fewer layers need backward-pass activation memory retained across the checkpointing boundaries), so this combination carries negligible OOM risk.
